fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not identify the specific transition-enabling material: the λ = 16 nm semicoherent FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer.
It replaces room-temperature nanoindentation experiments on sputtered coatings with an unsupported high-temperature molecular-dynamics scenario.
It omits the crucial role of misfit dislocations at semicoherent interfaces, including dislocation blocking, pileup, localized stress, and proposed interfacial amorphization.
It provides no mechanism-resolving outcome such as stress exponents or comparison with coherent M8 and grain-boundary-dominated M32/M80 samples.
explanation: The response recognizes interface coherency as relevant and mentions a transition between diffusion- and dislocation-mediated creep, but largely restates the question. It fails to name the Al-Cr-Fe-Ni M16 multilayer or explain why its semicoherent interfaces produce the transition. Its MD intervention, 800 K condition, baseline, and simulation boundaries do not match the target study. The proposed measurements are only weakly discriminating because creep rate and dislocation density alone do not establish atomic diffusion or interface slip, and no supporting evidence is supplied.
